agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: I use VS Code for all my coding with Claude Code as an extension.

also.quote: I don’t plan on trying anything other than Claude Code, there is still so much to master.

history.quote: I’ve gone through two epoch moments with these tools, the first was adopting Cursor as my text editor.

Claude Code is a background app which runs in the terminal which is sortof a long-running connection to an LLM which can do very long running tasks and has a sense of how to verify things in the way that you would when writing code.

agents.name: Claude Code on the web
agents.quote: I've been trying to use the new scheduled claude code (web) features to do this, so far it's caught a few typos and links

models.name: Fable
models.quote: For most of the year, the models themselves have come and gone. I didn’t really think much about them. This changed with Fable, which I think was a significant jump in capabilities.

history.quote: I’m finding myself using Claude Code almost every time I open up my editor, and it’s capabilities feels to have had quite a boost with the introduction of Sonnet 4.5.

review_style.value: Reads all Puzzmo code; Claude reviews every PR too
review_style.quote: I give pretty specific instructions, read all the code for Puzzmo systems and am very present in reviewing the output of an LLM but every line of code used to be a journey and now it’s a transaction.

also.quote: Yeah, I am definitely the one making that pile bigger and so I have to triple review my own PRs nowadays!

I have Claude automatically review all Pull Requests in Puzzmo. For me, this is my main review partner on a pull request (outside of future me) - I’ve found it to be a good ‘you missed this’ sorta review, but it is sorta marking itself and so reviews have a tendency to be ‘This is great.’

harness.value: VS Code with the Claude Code extension, multiple clones of the monorepo instead of worktrees
harness.quote: I still operate with multiple clones, though I’ve raised my limit to 3 clones of the Puzzmo monorepo.

history.value: Two clones, different VS Code profiles
history.quote: Anthropic have information about how to use worktrees - I would like to argue for a simpler approach. Two clones, different VS Code profiles.

parallelism.quote: I still operate with multiple clones, though I’ve raised my limit to 3 clones of the Puzzmo monorepo.

history.quote: Two clones, different VS Code profiles.

rules_files.quote: - Do not push to remote or deploy unless explicitly asked.

signature.caption: human writes the headline
signature.why: Our pick: he types the first line of every commit himself and Claude only adds the body from the diff, so humans still write for humans.
signature.quote: The argument to `/commit` is the first line of the commit message. Use it verbatim — no reformatting, no conventional-commit prefix, no capitalization fixes. If there is no argument, stop and ask the user for one; the point of this skill is that the human writes the headline.

archetype.why: One harness in his editor, no MCP, and he reads all the Puzzmo code himself.
